sentences.text: Sveltonectes is an extinct genus of ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaurs from the Early Cretaceous of western Russia. The specific name means "unusual" and refers to the animal's numerous unusual features and tooth morphology.
It is unique among its relatives for having small, sharp teeth and a very primitive prootic bone.

The genus is known from holotype IRSNB R269, an almost complete skeleton with a partial skull preserved in three dimensions. The genus was named by Fischer, Masure, Arkhangelsky, and Godefroit in 2011, with Sveltonectes insolitus as the type species.

Phylogenetic analysis places Sveltonectes as most closely related to Aegirosaurus within the family Ophthalmosauridae. It is classified within the subfamily Platypterygiinae of the family Ophthalmosauridae.
Fossils date to the late Barremian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 126 million years ago. The time range for the genus is estimated between 125.77 and 121.4 million years ago.
